title: Developer Cost Sandbox: onboarding, experiments, and fidelity playbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary
This document describes the Developer Cost Sandbox: a self-serve environment and playbook that lets engineering and product teams run realistic consumption experiments, validate fidelity/cost tradeoffs, and prototype onboarding flows with sample pricing and SLO mappings. The sandbox is intended for: developer teams evaluating Redwood features, partner integrators running pricing experiments, and internal product teams validating fidelity gating logic before customer rollouts.

Objectives
- Provide a low-friction, instrumented sandbox that simulates production consumption economics with tunable parameters (batching, kv-cache retention, quantization profile).
- Enable safe experimentation for developer and partner cohorts without impacting billing or tenant SLAs.
- Surface observability, cost delta signals, and fidelity regressions tied to prompt sets and sample workloads.
- Offer a prescriptive onboarding checklist that reduces migration friction from Hosted -> Dedicated.

Target personas
- Developer (PLG): trying API prototypes and needs quick cost visibility.
- Platform/Partner engineer: validating variant rollouts and warm-capacity assumptions.
- Product manager: running pricing experiments and SLO tradeoff analysis.

Scope and non-goals
- In scope: simulated per-token cost modeling, fidelity presets, telemetry enrichment, preconfigured prompt sets, sample pricing tiers, and an experimentation API.
- Out of scope: charging live invoices for sandbox activity, full multi-tenant isolation for Dedicated customers, and long-term retention of evaluation telemetry beyond 30 days.

Success metrics (OKRs)
1) Time to first meaningful cost insight: <= 15 minutes for a new user to run sample workload and see cost/fidelity delta.
2) Experiment completion rate: 60% of started experiments produce a fidelity / cost report within one week.
3) Migration impact: 15% reduction in customer-reported onboarding friction (measured by NPS follow-ups) for customers who used the sandbox.

High-level product requirements (PRD items)
1. Sandbox environment provisioning API
   - Endpoint: POST /v1/sandbox-provision
   - Inputs: tenant_id (sandbox), preset_profile (dev | partner | fast-latency | high-throughput), duration_days (1-30)
   - Response: sandbox_id, endpoints, temporary_api_key, telemetry_dashboard_link
   - Ownership: onboarding-service (product)

2. Fidelity presets and toggles
   - Presets: dev (base), low-cost-quant (8-bit), kv-extended (retain prefixes for 10s), high-throughput-batching (2x batch window)
   - UI toggles available in sandbox console and via API.
   - Each toggle must emit a configuration event to telemetry for correlation.

3. Cost emulator and estimator
   - Offline estimator that uses production kernel profiles to compute estimated per-token cost given a preset and workload.
   - Real-time estimator that approximates cost during streaming responses with per-minute accuracy +/-10%.
   - Outputs: estimated_cost_usd, estimated_tail_latency_ms, effective_throughput_rps.

4. Fidelity regression detection
   - Shadow evaluation harness: run sample prompt-set against baseline and candidate preset, compute metrics: ROUGE-L, semantic-similarity (embedding cosine), hallucination-score (heuristic).
   - Flag experiments with >5% drop in semantic-similarity or >2x hallucination delta.

5. Experiment report and export
   - Generate PDF/JSON report containing configuration, telemetry graphs, cost breakdown by token type, example model outputs (anonymized), and change recommendations.
   - Export formats: PDF, JSON, CSV.

6. Safety and billing guardrails
   - Sandbox API keys are rate-limited to 10 rps and capped at 10k tokens/day per sandbox by default.
   - Sandbox activity should never incur live billing. Any attempt is routed to a simulated billing queue and flagged.

Telemetry and observability requirements
- Telemetry events required: sandbox.provision, sandbox.config.update, sandbox.run.start, sandbox.run.finish, sandbox.estimate.cost, sandbox.eval.result.
- Essential fields for each event: sandbox_id, preset, user_id_anonymized, timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, estimated_cost_usd, actual_cost_delta_usd, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, fidelity_metrics (as JSON string).
- Retention: 30 days for full-resolution, 12 months aggregated (daily) for product analytics.

Design constraints and considerations
- Runtime parity: sandbox must use the same kernel selection and quantization codepaths as production variants to ensure meaningful cost deltas. However, sandbox may use smaller GPU instances to keep infrastructure cost down.
- Deterministic prompt-sets: provide curated prompt collections (smalltalk, summarization, retrieval-augmented, code-generation) to ensure comparable fidelity metrics across experiments.
- Privacy: sample outputs included in reports must be redacted for PII by default; PII redaction is an opt-in toggle requiring compliance approval.

UX and Console flow (high level)
1) Provision sandbox via quickstart wizard or API.
2) Select preset or assemble toggles.
3) Upload or select a prompt-set and a sample traffic profile (burst, steady, conversational).
4) Run experiment (single job or scheduled cohort).
5) Inspect sample outputs, fidelity metrics, cost breakdown, and suggested configuration changes.
6) Export report and open a migration checklist if migration to Dedicated or Private is desired.

Example CLI flow
$ redwood sandbox create --preset=dev --duration=7 --name="acme-dev-eval"
Provisioned sandbox: sandbox_abc123
Temporary key saved to ~/.redwood/sandbox_keys/sandbox_abc123.key
$ redwood sandbox run --sandbox=sandbox_abc123 --promptset=summarization-small --traffic=steady-10m
Experiment queued: job_20260409_001

Programmatic experiment configuration (example JSON payload)
{
  "sandbox_id": "sandbox_abc123",
  "preset": "low-cost-quant",
  "prompt_set": "retrieval-smoke",
  "traffic_profile": "burst-1m",
  "eval_runs": 10
}

Pricing and packaging experiments matrix
| Experiment name | Preset | Pricing knob | Hypothesis | Success threshold | Duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dev-fast-tiling | high-throughput-batching | per-minute session credits | batching reduces unit cost by >=25% with <10% p95 latency increase | pass if cost delta >=25% and p95 latency increase <=10% | 7 days |
| quant-fidelity-check | low-cost-quant | fidelity surcharge vs baseline | 8-bit quant reduces cost by >=30% but fidelity drop <=3% | pass if semantic-similarity drop <=3% | 14 days |
| kv-affinity | kv-extended | session-duration credit | extended KV reduces tokens by caching prefixes for active sessions | pass if effective tokens_saved >= 15% | 10 days |

Rollout plan and staging
- Alpha (internal only): feature gated for internal product and solutions engineers. Expect manual provisioning and close support.
- Beta (selected customers + partners): self-serve provisioning with expanded presets and sandbox quotas. Collect feedback on report usefulness and gating UX.
- GA: open to all developers; integrate sandbox into onboarding flow and console trial credit redemption.

Risks and mitigation
- False cost signals: mitigate by calibrating emulator with production kernel telemetry monthly. Add a confidence band to estimators.
- Overfitting to prompt-sets: provide diverse, rotating prompt collections and allow customers to bring their own sets for evaluation.
- Accidental billing exposure: keep sandbox billing paths simulated; automated audits on sandbox->production configuration changes.

Operational playbook (Day-2)
1) Monitoring: dashboards for sandbox provision rate, sandbox churn, median experiment runtime, and estimator error vs production.
2) Alerts: estimator error > 20% (sev-2), sandbox quota exhaustion spikes (sev-3).
3) Support flow: staged escalation to Onboarding SRE -> Product -> Solutions Eng. Provide a postmortem template for failed experiments.

Ownership and stakeholders
- Product owner: Priya Nair (product)
- Engineering owner: Runtime onboarding-service team (eng-platform); lead: Evan Brooks
- Telemetry and analytics: Observability team; lead: Lucia Gomez
- Solutions and partner onboarding: Customer Success; contact: Marta Ivanova

  "sandbox_id": "sandbox_abc123",

}

Appendix B — Migration checklist (quick)
1) Export experiment report and attach to account migration ticket.
2) Confirm estimated production-cost delta and select target fidelity package.
3) Schedule canary rollout on Dedicated: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on fidelity regressions.
4) Validate SLO mapping and billing hooks with finance and revrec.

Notes and open questions
- Should sandbox output storage be retained beyond 30 days for enterprise trials? (privacy + cost tradeoff)
- How to best correlate sandbox estimator errors to GPU kernel and sequence-length distributions? (instrumentation work needed)
